The workshop starts before sunrise because the old presses need time to warm. I unlock the side
door, set my lunch beside the sink, and check yesterday's notes. One roller still squeaks. It has
done that since March, despite oil, patience, and two increasingly confident repairs. By eight the
first sheets are drying on the rack. Their blue is a little darker than planned, but the customer
likes it. We talk through the next run, mark a correction in pencil, and agree to leave the final
choice until daylight reaches the back table.
